blocked.reason: School grounds. CLAUDE.md hard rule 10 ships a tree on school grounds only where there is real evidence the grounds are genuinely open (a public path crossing them, a public park the school merely borders, open at weekends). The register's bezoekbaar=ja flag is the only evidence we have, and it is not enough to write an honest access line for a private school garden behind a house on the Nassaulaan. Held as a lead, not rejected: one confirmation that the garden is open, or that the beech is visible from public ground on the Nassaulaan, unblocks it as a view-only entry with the pin on the viewing place.

notes.what: Its approximate pin (52.0838873,4.3225274) sits beside the register's 'Zomereiken Hertenkamp', a group of SEVENTEEN oaks planted 1700-1750, which also matches our stated age of about 300 years. hag_006, added the same day, is the register's separate SINGLE oak 193 m east at the Bezuidenhoutseweg end, band 1750-1800. So they are two different trees and were correctly written as two.
notes.but: If hag_002 is one of the seventeen rather than a distinguishable individual, it fails the collectible-point test and should become one entry describing the Hertenkamp oaks, or be repinned onto whichever oak the story is actually about. Needs eyes on the Koekamp or a source naming an individual tree. Not touched by this pass.
